program_overview.title: Game Development for Kids
program_overview.tagline: From playing games to making them: real Scratch games first, then Roblox and Minecraft worlds, finished and shown off in six honest months.
program_overview.description:
Every child who loves games has the same secret wish: to make one. This live online course grants it properly for ages 8 to 12: game logic learned in Scratch, where scores, lives, levels and enemy behavior are built by the child, then complete 2D games polished until friends ask to play again, and finally the leap into 3D worlds with Roblox Studio and coded Minecraft builds, plus first multiplayer fun.

Finishing is the discipline: every month ends with a playable build and a mixed challenge that quietly revises earlier skills, and the course ends with a capstone game, planned, built, playtested and presented at demo day. There is no monetization talk, no in-game purchase strategy and no chatbot dependence in this course; children this age should be building skill and joy, and that is the whole syllabus.

The pace is honest and kid-sized: six months at two live classes a week plus two to three hours of playful practice, with two more months in hand when needed. A final exam, capstone demo plus a friendly viva, decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision. Real games, real pride, depth over dopamine.

faqs.question: What games will my child actually make?
faqs.answer: Fifteen-plus playable builds across six months: complete Scratch games with scores, lives and enemies in the first two months, polished 2D games with levels and difficulty curves by month four, then a Roblox Studio world, a coded Minecraft build and first multiplayer fun, ending with a capstone game in the child’s chosen world, playtested and presented at demo day.

faqs.question: What age is right for this course?
faqs.answer: Ages 8 to 12, with batches grouped by age. Eight-year-olds thrive in the Scratch months and grow into the 3D tools; eleven and twelve-year-olds move faster and go deeper in Roblox and Minecraft. No coding background is needed.

faqs.question: How long does it take a child to learn game development?
faqs.answer: Six months at 2 live classes a week plus 2 to 3 hours of playful practice takes a child from first mechanic to a demo-day capstone. The course keeps two more months in hand for children who need more repetition, no rushing and no penalty. The first working game exists within the first month.

faqs.question: How is my child assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No, and it is all gentle: a small build after every class, a mixed challenge at the end of every month that revisits earlier skills, and a final exam at the end, a capstone demo plus a friendly viva and short quiz. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Does this course talk about making money from games?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. There is no monetization talk, no in-game purchase mechanics and no marketing lessons for children; those topics do not belong at 8 to 12. The course is about skill and joy: building games worth playing and finishing what you start. Sharing happens safely, with parent-managed accounts.

faqs.question: Are Roblox and Minecraft really educational?
faqs.answer: As building tools, genuinely yes: Roblox Studio teaches world design and first scripting, and coded Minecraft teaches logic and automation, both on platforms children already love, which makes the motivation free. The course uses them as classrooms, with accounts set up alongside a parent and sharing kept safe.

faqs.question: Is any paid software needed?
faqs.answer: No. Scratch is free, Roblox Studio is free to build with, and the Minecraft coding tools used in class are free. Any reasonably recent computer or laptop is enough.

faqs.question: What are the fees?

A mini batch of 3-4 children is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International families pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial class?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Your child will build a tiny game mechanic inside the demo itself.

faqs.question: Are classes live or recorded?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small groups with a real teacher, never pre-recorded videos. Children build during class and get unstuck on the spot, which is exactly what keeps game-making joyful instead of frustrating.
